_comment: The static libraries sherpa-onnx-sys links into the CandidCue binary, and
what each one IS. sbom/native-inputs.json records their digests; this
records their identity, because a digest says a file did not change and
nothing at all about whose work it is or on what terms.
Every file in native-inputs.json must be claimed by exactly one entry here.
scripts/generate-notices.mjs refuses otherwise: a native library nobody
classified is precisely the component an automated dependency scan misses,
because it is in neither lockfile.
`forbiddenInProprietaryBinary` means no code of it may reach the shipped
binary. `copyleftIfLinkedWith` means a component whose own licence governs
UNLESS the named copyleft projects ship beside it. Both are enforced against
a real ld64 linker map by scripts/verify-no-copyleft-objects.mjs — which is
the point: whether a binary is a derivative work is a fact about that
binary, not an argument about intentions.
`source` is the copy that was actually built, which is often not `upstream`
(the canonical project): `repository` and the tag or commit (`revision`) the
build pinned, the `archive` it fetched and that archive's `sha256`, the build
file that pins it (`pinnedBy`), and the `licenceFile` read at that revision.
`path` marks a work vendored inside `repository` rather than a fork of
`upstream`; `prebuiltBy` names whoever compiled an input that arrives as a
binary; `noticeFile` is a further notices file published at that revision.
A review that cannot say which source it read is not one, so both
generate-notices.mjs and verify-native-review.mjs refuse `reviewed: true`
without a repository and a revision.
`embeds` are third-party works compiled INTO a component's libraries:
header-only or vendored code under its own licence and authors. They claim
no library, so the one-owner rule above is untouched, and the notices name
each one beside the component that carries it.
`evidence` records what the SPDX id is based on. `reviewed` stays false
until a HUMAN confirms it and accepts it for a proprietary, statically
linked, signed distribution; scripts/verify-native-review.mjs refuses a
release while any is false. It is a step of release-verify.mjs that only a
full run reaches, so CI never runs it and a tagged release cannot skip it.

components.note: The inference runtime CandidCue calls. Its own licence text also travels with each installed model's ATTRIBUTION.md.
components.evidence: Apache-2.0 confirmed from the unpacked sherpa-onnx-sys 1.13.4 manifest and the LICENSE in the crate. Provenance, 2026-10-17: sherpa-onnx-sys 1.13.4's build.rs downloads the release v1.13.4 assets (tag v1.13.4 is commit 142807252687d81b40d6315f23470a1512a00de3). That tag's .github/workflows/macos.yaml configures ONE universal2 static Release build (CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES="arm64;x86_64", SHERPA_ONNX_ENABLE_TTS=ON) and `lipo -thin`s every library into sherpa-onnx-v1.13.4-osx-arm64-static-lib.tar.bz2 (sha256 57801db2bbb786a5d343f515a38ff210b401842338bdc804fa075312d1cd2404) and -osx-x64-static-lib.tar.bz2 (sha256 2bda2c10b31a1cfc45d9f9e14bd4983743ec3779d309e42d99a6c8fa1689043f), so both slices come from one configure and share every source pin recorded below; the archives the build fetched match the published assets byte for byte. Three archives this entry used to claim carry sherpa-onnx's name and are other projects' work: libsherpa-onnx-fst.a and libsherpa-onnx-fstfar.a (OpenFst) and libsherpa-onnx-kaldifst-core.a (kaldifst) now have entries of their own. Not audited here: header-only code sherpa-onnx's own CMakeLists fetches into these three libraries (cmake/json.cmake, cmake/hclust-cpp.cmake).

components.note: Weighted finite-state transducers for the decoder. sherpa-onnx builds them from a fork and gives the libraries its own name; the code is the OpenFst authors' (Google LLC).
components.evidence: Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned tag. sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/openfst.cmake fetches the archive above (sha256 verified by download) and sets OUTPUT_NAME sherpa-onnx-fst / sherpa-onnx-fstfar, which is why these archives carry sherpa-onnx's name. COPYING at that tag is the Apache-2.0 grant, "Copyright 2005-2026 Google LLC"; src/lib/fst.cc carries the same Apache header. Previously claimed by the sherpa-onnx entry under sherpa-onnx's licence, which was the right licence and the wrong authors.

embeds.evidence: "a modified version of the std::basic_filebuf from libc++", copied through Kaldi, and included by kaldi-io.cc via kaldi-pipebuf.h; kaldifst::basic_filebuf symbols are in libsherpa-onnx-kaldifst-core.a. The header says it is "dual licensed under the MIT and the University of Illinois Open Source License licenses" and carries both texts at its end.

components.note: Kaldi's finite-state-transducer utilities on top of OpenFst. kaldi-decoder fetches it; sherpa-onnx renames the library.
components.evidence: Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned tag. kaldi-decoder v0.3.0's cmake/kaldifst.cmake fetches the archive above (sha256 verified by download); sherpa-onnx ships no kaldifst.cmake of its own, so that is the file CMake resolves, and sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/kaldi-decoder.cmake renames the kaldifst_core target to sherpa-onnx-kaldifst-core. LICENSE at v1.8.0 is Apache-2.0 under Kaldi's "authors own their contributions" preamble. Most kaldifst/csrc files are copied from Kaldi and carry its copyright lines with no per-file licence, so that LICENSE governs them; the few with a header carry Apache-2.0's. The exception is basic-filebuf.h, recorded under `embeds`. Previously claimed by the sherpa-onnx entry.

components.note: A binary build of ONNX Runtime v1.27.0, compiled by a sherpa-onnx maintainer and vendored into the sherpa-onnx archive. It compiles in third-party code of its own — protobuf, abseil, Eigen and others.
components.evidence: Confirmed 2026-10-17. sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/onnxruntime.cmake selects onnxruntime-osx-universal-static.cmake for a universal static build, which fetches the zip above; its sha256 was verified by download, and `lipo -thin arm64` of the libonnxruntime.a inside it reproduces the digest recorded in sbom/native-inputs.json exactly. The library names its own source: it contains "ORT Build Info: git-branch=HEAD, git-commit-id=8f0278c77", and microsoft/onnxruntime tag v1.27.0 is commit 8f0278c77bf44b0cc83c098c6c722b92a36ac4b5; its compiled-in paths are under onnxruntime-build/onnxruntime/, the checkout csukuangfj/onnxruntime-build builds from. LICENSE at v1.27.0 is MIT (Microsoft Corporation). The zip carries no licence file. ThirdPartyNotices.txt at the same tag covers the third-party code compiled into ONNX Runtime; this review links it rather than itemising it.

embeds.evidence: Header-only; kaldi-decoder's sources instantiate it, and Eigen template symbols are in libkaldi-decoder-core.a. kaldi-decoder v0.3.0's CMakeLists calls include(eigen), and it is sherpa-onnx's cmake/eigen.cmake that answers, not kaldi-decoder's own (which pins 3.4.0): sherpa-onnx's cmake/ directory is earlier in CMAKE_MODULE_PATH. That file pins 5.0.1, sha256 verified by download. COPYING.README at 5.0.1: "Eigen is primarily MPL2 licensed"; the other COPYING files there are Apache, BSD and MINPACK, with no LGPL or GPL.

components.evidence: Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned tag. sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/kaldi-decoder.cmake fetches the archive above (sha256 verified by download), and the library's compiled-in paths are under _deps/kaldi_decoder-src/. LICENSE at v0.3.0 is Apache-2.0. It used to share an entry with kaldi-native-fbank, which is a separate project from a separate repository.

Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned tag (commit b09e686fe2084732ddd30d1ef80acfc0f13eaf01). sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/kaldi-native-fbank.cmake fetches the archive above (sha256 verified by download). LICENSE at v1.22.3 is Apache-2.0, and its sources carry Apache headers. It brings KISS FFT with it, which has its own entry.

components.note: The FFT behind feature extraction, fetched by kaldi-native-fbank. This copy is BSD-3-Clause; the Unlicense also in its LICENSES directory covers only test files, which are not compiled.
components.evidence: Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned commit. kaldi-native-fbank v1.22.3's own cmake/kissfft.cmake fetches the archive above (sha256 verified by download); sherpa-onnx has no kissfft.cmake. COPYING there reads "SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause" and points at LICENSES/BSD-3-Clause, and every compiled source (kiss_fft.c, kiss_fftr.c and their headers) carries a BSD-3-Clause header. LICENSES/Unlicense applies to test/ only. No LGPL or GPL text anywhere in the tree: the LGPL/GPL history belongs to the copy vendored into Eigen, which this is not.

embeds.evidence: Header-only, vendored as ssentencepiece/csrc/darts.h (DARTS_VERSION "0.32"), "taken from https://github.com/s-yata/darts-clone". The BSD 2-clause licence is written into the header itself: "Copyright (c) 2008-2014, Susumu Yata". Its symbols are in libssentencepiece_core.a.

components.note: Tokenisation. The library is called ssentencepiece; the project is simple-sentencepiece.
components.evidence: Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned tag. sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/simple-sentencepiece.cmake fetches the archive above (sha256 verified by download), and the library's compiled-in paths are under _deps/simple-sentencepiece-src/. LICENSE at v0.7 is Apache-2.0, and its sources carry Apache headers. This entry used to name https://github.com/pkufool/ssentencepiece, which does not exist.

components.note: In the archive and on the link line, but CandidCue captures audio in the renderer and never calls it, and none of its code survives dead-stripping. The PortAudio community's requests that accompany its licence are, in its own words, non-binding.
components.evidence: Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the release tarball. sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/portaudio.cmake fetches the archive above (sha256 verified by download). The library names its own source: "PortAudio V19.7.0-devel, revision 147dd722548358763a8b649b3e4b41dfffbcfbb6", which is PortAudio/portaudio tag v19.7.0. LICENSE.txt is the MIT grant (Ross Bencina and Phil Burk) followed by "The text above constitutes the entire PortAudio license; however, the PortAudio community also makes the following non-binding requests". Measured: no PortAudio code survives dead-stripping either.

embeds.evidence: The amalgamated header src/uni_algo.h (UNI_ALGO_CPP_LIB_VERSION 8001, i.e. 0.8.1) is included by src/phonemize.cpp, one of the three sources of the piper_phonemize library. Its own notice: "License: Public Domain or MIT - choose whatever you want"; licenses/uni-algo/LICENSE.md is the public-domain (Unlicense) text, and the MIT text is at the end of the header.

components.note: Declares MIT. The reason it is often called GPL is that it CALLS espeak_TextToPhonemesWithTerminator, so a binary containing both piper's code and eSpeak's is distributed on eSpeak's terms. That is a statement about a binary, not about piper — and `verify-no-copyleft-objects.mjs` measures which binary we have. In CandidCue's, two of piper's own symbols survive (its translation-unit static initialiser and piper::DEFAULT_PHONEME_MAP, about 416 bytes) and NO eSpeak code does. So piper's own MIT terms are the operative ones, and MIT is satisfied by the attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. `copyleftIfLinkedWith` is what makes that conditional machine-checked rather than an argument somebody remembers: the day eSpeak or ucd code appears alongside it, this becomes a failure.
components.evidence: MIT declared upstream. Measured 2026-08-13 by scripts/verify-no-copyleft-objects.mjs against an arm64 linker map: 2 of its own symbols ship (__GLOBAL__sub_I_phonemize.cpp and piper::DEFAULT_PHONEME_MAP), and no eSpeak NG or ucd-tools code ships beside them. Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned commit: sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/piper-phonemize.cmake fetches the archive above from the csukuangfj fork (sha256 verified by download). LICENSE.md there is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2023 Michael Hansen", byte-identical to rhasspy/piper-phonemize's. The fork's own CMakeLists would fetch a second eSpeak NG when ESPEAK_NG_DIR is unset; sherpa-onnx's CMakeLists sets it to the eSpeak NG source below, so it links that copy and no other.

components.note: The Unicode character-database TOOLS, not the UCD data. The data tables are Unicode-DFS-2016; Reece Dunn's wrapper — which is what libucd.a is — is GPL-3.0-or-later. It arrives with eSpeak NG and goes out the same way.
components.evidence: GPL-3.0-or-later (rhdunn/ucd-tools; the wrapper, not the Unicode data). Measured 2026-08-13: every object the linker loaded from it was dead-stripped; nothing of it is in the binary. Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned commit: it is not fetched on its own but vendored in the eSpeak NG fork at src/ucd-tools, and sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/espeak-ng-for-piper.cmake installs its `ucd` target. src/ucd-tools/COPYING there is GPL version 3; src/ctype.c and the generated tables (src/categories.c and the rest) carry Reece H. Dunn's "either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version" header; README.md: "UCD Tools is released under the GPL version 3 or later license", with the Unicode data files under the Unicode terms in COPYING.UCD.

components.note: The one that matters. sherpa-onnx-sys puts -lespeak-ng on the link line of every build (SHERPA_ONNX_STATIC_LIBS in its build.rs) and there is no feature or env var that removes it; the `shared` alternative is worse, because the sherpa-onnx dylib genuinely contains this code. k2-fsa acknowledge the incompatibility with their own Apache-2.0 and plan to drop espeak-ng and piper-phonemize in a 2.0. The source-build mitigation, -DSHERPA_ONNX_ENABLE_TTS=OFF, is unavailable to us because we consume their prebuilt archive. So the position is: nothing references an eSpeak symbol, a selective static link extracts no object file, and no GPL code is in the binary — which is an argument until `verify-no-copyleft-objects.mjs` turns it into a linker-map fact.
components.evidence: GPL-3.0-or-later. Measured 2026-08-13 against an arm64 linker map: the linker LOADS 23 of its 27 objects, because libsherpa-onnx-c-api.a is one broad object with undefined references to OfflineTts — but dead-stripping removes all of it. What survives is 28 coalesced literals ("UTF-8", "%s", numeric pool entries) and no eSpeak code or data whatsoever. Confirmed 2026-10-17 against the source at the pinned commit: sherpa-onnx v1.13.4's cmake/espeak-ng-for-piper.cmake fetches the csukuangfj fork above (sha256 verified by download) and installs its espeak-ng target. COPYING there is GPL version 3, README.md says "GPL version 3 or later", and the compiled library sources (src/libespeak-ng/speech.c and the rest) carry the or-later header; the one that does not, sPlayer.c, is compiled only with USE_SPEECHPLAYER, which sherpa-onnx turns off. The fork's top-level COPYING.APACHE, COPYING.BSD2 and COPYING.UCD cover individual files within it; none makes the library as a whole anything but GPL-3.0-or-later.
